column1: # The 61 results-call transcripts that tables/results_calls_word_census.tsv counts words in, one row per call: the calls that eight Chinese companies held from Feb 18, 2025 to Nov 19, 2026 (Alibaba, Baidu, JD.com, Kuaishou and Tencent, 8 calls each; Kingsoft Cloud, Meituan and Xiaomi, 7 each). The list was made on Nov 23, 2026; every row was checked against its saved page by script on Nov 25, 2026. Columns: the company; the call as the page labels it (the transcript site labels a call by the company's own fiscal quarter, so Alibaba's call of Nov 19, 2026 is Q2 2027; Alibaba's own transcripts name the quarter by its last month); the date of the call; the saved id; the site that carries the transcript (stockanalysis.com for 54 calls; Alibaba's own investor site, data.alibabagroup.com, for 7, each a PDF); where the page says the transcript is from (each of the 54 pages names Quartr as its source, in the words "Earnings call transcripts are provided by Quartr and are published within hours after each earnings call."; the 7 are the company's own transcripts); whether the page marks any part of the transcript as made, translated or arranged by a model or a machine; and the number of markers of a passage that is not translated, [Foreign language] or [Non-English content] in any spacing or spelling, within its two square brackets, in the transcript as the page shows it; two markers whose opening bracket is missing or misprinted are not counted ("Non-English content]" with no opening bracket, in Kuaishou's call of May 27, 2026, and "Foreign language]" opened by a curly brace, in Meituan's of May 26, 2025). On a model or a machine: no for all 61. None of the 61 saved pages carries such a note, in its markup or in its plain text (for the 7 PDFs, in their text), and the 54 pages do not say how Quartr makes its transcripts; controls: the same test finds the note on a saved Chinese machine translation of one of these calls, whose page says so [cn-ga31-callszh-9], and in two planted sentences, and does not take a speaker's words on code written by AI for one. On passages not translated: 27 of the 61 transcripts hold at least one marker (Kuaishou 8, JD.com 7, Kingsoft Cloud 6, Meituan 5, Alibaba 1; 574 markers in all, from 1 to 38 in a transcript). The word census counts 25 of the 27, because its row looks for the two usual spellings and so passes over JD.com's call of Aug 13, 2026 ("[Non-English cont ent]") and Meituan's of Nov 28, 2025 ("[ Foreign language]"). What the table is not: the transcripts were not checked against the recordings, so a word, a figure or a speaker's label in them may be wrong (in 20 of the 54 some turns are headed only Speaker and a number); the absence of a note about a model does not show that none was used; and the list is of the calls read for the word census, not of every call these companies held.
